product: FIRBENCH-1 benchmark tool: static private FIR bench report (S1 to S8) and the occlusion label queue (L1)
goals: Every verdict shows its admissibility, n_eff, MDE and interval. A result that is unratified, inconclusive or unresolvable names no winner.
An operator can find where faces are lost, from the verdict to the stage, then to the failing faces, without losing sort, filter or position.
Incompatible runs are refused with a reason before any difference is computed.
The label queue shows the annotator only what labelling from pixels needs, and no internal item role.

jobs.label: Decide whether a model change is real

screens.title: S1 Verdict
screens.purpose: Answers whether the model change is real at the primary point (FNIR at FPIR 0.01, end to end, misses count). Shows the verdict only with its admissibility, n_eff, MDE and interval. Bench states: unratified and inconclusive are degraded; unresolvable_fpir is degraded and its verdict reason is primary_fpir_unresolvable. None of them names a winner.

zones.label: Verdict line: question, paired difference Δ(B−A) or per-leg state with its interval, PSU n_eff and deff. superior ✓ and non-inferior ✓ name a winner only when ratified and sealed. inconclusive ○ (degraded) prints INCONCLUSIVE and the InconclusiveReason value verbatim (primary_fpir_unresolvable, required_guardrail_unscored, margin_unreachable_mde_gt_delta, non_confirmatory_frame or insufficient_independent_psus). unratified ○ (degraded) prints the numbers and 'unratified: no verdict'. unresolvable_fpir ○ (degraded) prints primary_fpir_unresolvable and names no winner. A hypothesis not reached prints 'not evaluated'. Serves VIZ-23, INT-22.
Admissibility line: frame id and tag (diagnostic, development or confirmatory), frame-inspected flag, n_eff, deff, and MDE per step. Every number carries its frame's tag. Serves VIZ-23.
FNIR at FPIR 0.01 per leg (SF-128, AF-512, and the IF judge row) as a dot-range with its interval and the frozen τ. Each leg labelled directly, not by legend. Serves VIZ-40, VIZ-23.

Exact-lookup table: per leg FNIR at FPIR 0.01, FPIR measured with its UCL, frozen τ, and stage counts. Same numbers as the range. Unratified rows show numbers with 'unratified: no verdict' (degraded). Serves VIZ-32.

Guardrail veto table: false names per 1k mentions, worst pair-cell FNIR floor, worst cohort FPIR, p95 ms per face. Each row shows its rule (≤ sealed, floor or budget) and a mark: ✓ pass, ✗ veto, ○ unscored or unresolvable (cohort n_eff under 3/FPIR). A null or unscored veto is inconclusive with required_guardrail_unscored (degraded). Serves INT-22, VIZ-32.
Tabs: Curves, Pair cells, Stages, Failures, Clusters, Compare, Frames and power. Each tab is a keyboard-reachable anchor after a skip link. Switching tabs keeps the run. Serves INT-25.

screens.title: S2 Operating curves
screens.purpose: FNIR against FPIR on a log scale for each leg, with τ frozen on calibration folds and the test set read once. Bench states: unresolvable_fpir is degraded, for the region below 3/n_eff; unratified is degraded, with numbers only and no winner. Chart treatment follows the actual rendered marks and task: [VIZ-35] Use a range-frame for observed extrema (The Visual Display of Quantitative Information, ch. 6) applies only to a bivariate-pattern scatterplot whose decision-relevant measured extrema are hidden by unneeded round-number frame tails. Trim those tails and label the extrema, retaining required references, scales, units, legibility and marginal views. No blanket mandate or ban covers S1–S8; chart names alone do not decide applicability. FPIR reference lines at 0.001, 0.01 and 0.05 remain.

zones.label: Operating curves per leg on a log FPIR axis, with reference lines at FPIR 0.001, 0.01 and 0.05 and a direct label on each curve. Points below 3/n_eff are shaded (░) and marked ○ unresolvable, and no FNIR claim is drawn inside that region (degraded). A curve with no data reads 'no data' (empty). Serves VIZ-40, VIZ-27.

At-τ table: per leg FNIR, FPIR measured with its UCL, false accepts as an integer over non-mated source units, and the gallery identity count. Same numbers as the τ marker on the curve. Serves VIZ-32, INT-22.
Explore τ is a mode. A banner reads 'exploring τ: nothing is saved'. Dev frames only; sealed frames are read-only. Leaving the mode restores the frozen τ and its values. Serves INT-23, INT-21.

screens.title: S3 Pair cells
screens.purpose: Query by enrolled occluder cell, with FNIR at τ per leg and the faces, identities and PSUs in each cell. Bench states: unratified shows the cell numbers with 'unratified: no verdict' (degraded). An empty cell is 'collect', not an error.

zones.label: Query by enrolled grid: FNIR at τ per leg (SF-128, AF-512) with n faces, identities and PSUs per cell. Real and synthetic occlusion sit in separate panes. A cell with fewer than 30 independent units reads 'not scored'. An empty cell reads '○ no data → collect'. Serves EVAL-20, VIZ-32.
Cell to failures for that cell and leg. Returning from failures restores this grid with sort, scroll and filter kept. Serves INT-25.

screens.title: S4 Stages
screens.purpose: Where each GT face ended in the end-to-end ledger, per leg, with the joint gaps against native. Rows are SearchStage values. Bench states: unratified shows the rows and gaps with 'unratified: no verdict' (degraded). The judge row shows no arm deltas.

zones.label: Stage waterfall as a table, in order: GT faces (exhaustive frame only), detected (IoU ≥ 0.50, one-to-one), aligned, top-1 correct identity, accepted at τ with the correct name. The fused leg has no unaligned row. Unavailable arm counts sit in their own arm_availability column, never as a stage. Serves VIZ-32, VIZ-23.

Joint gaps against native with paired PSU intervals for gt_crop_redetect and cached_yunet_landmark_replay, one row each, with the unavailable face count per arm. No shares are apportioned: these are joint intervention gaps, not causal effects. Serves VIZ-23, VIZ-32.
A stage row opens failures filtered to that stage, with the leg fixed. Back returns to this ledger. Serves INT-25.

screens.title: S5 Failures
screens.purpose: Failures for one query cell and one leg, with the selection pool stated before any face. Stage labels are FaceOutcome and SearchStage values. Bench states: unratified shows counts with 'unratified: no verdict' (degraded). No failure in the cell is empty, not an error.

zones.label: Selection pool, before any row: reuse the exhaustive frame inventory's overall image count and GT-face count, including existing mated/non-mated face counts and explicit unresolved identities. The source pool is fixed independently of detections; background source units are counted separately, never as GT faces. Show eligible images/faces after the current frame, sampling arm, query/enrolled cell, leg, stage and outcome filters; selected distinct images/faces in the displayed rows; and images actually shown as crops (0 when crops are off). Eligible/selected GT-face counts exclude detector-only rows; report detection counts and represented background-unit counts separately. Display the active filters, sort, offset, limit and omitted counts. Default: all eligible failure rows, no hidden cap, stable pseudonymous image_id then face_id order; any changed sort or limit is disclosed. Missing exhaustive GT reads 'pool not established'; it never implies admissible non-mated N. A selection is never shown without its pool. Serves [VIZ-41] Reveal the image-selection pool (Visual Explanations, ch. 1).
Outcome counts table: missed, unaligned, wrong_identity, rejected, false_accept. Each count is exact, and a nonzero row is marked ✗. Serves VIZ-32.

Failure table, one row per failing face: SearchStage reached, top-1 identity as a pseudonym, its score against τ, and its result on each other leg. Each row explicitly identifies its selected image_id and face_id with stable pseudonymous aliases; background detections identify their pseudonymous background source unit separately. Repeated faces from one image do not inflate the distinct-image count. Sort and filter controls are kept on return from pair cells. Only pseudonyms appear. Selection identities reconcile with pool-accounting. Serves VIZ-32, INT-25 and [VIZ-41] Reveal the image-selection pool (Visual Explanations, ch. 1).

Face crop, shown only when the run was written with include_crops. The output stays under benchmarks/private. Without it the zone reads 'crop off' (empty). Each displayed crop carries the same pseudonymous image_id and face_id as its failure row and links back to pool-accounting; shown-image counts count distinct images, with selected face/crop counts separate. Serves VIZ-23 and [VIZ-41] Reveal the image-selection pool (Visual Explanations, ch. 1).
Back to pair cells or to the stage ledger, whichever opened this view. Sort and filter are kept. Serves INT-25.

screens.title: S6 Compare
screens.purpose: Compares run B with a baseline run A on the same frame. Only compatible runs can be compared. An incompatible pair is refused with its reason and no difference is computed. Bench states: incompatible_runs is error (reason shown, no subtraction, exit to run A). unratified is degraded: numbers for A and B, 'unratified: no verdict', never a ▼ winner.

zones.label: Compatibility checks: frame, scorer boundary semantics, OpenCV and ORT versions, leg contracts. Each shows ✓ or ✗ with its reason. A changed leg contract is listed as expected or unexpected. The run B picker offers only runs that pass these checks. incompatible_runs is error: the reason is printed and no metric row shows. Serves INT-22, FORM-11.

Metric table: A, B and Δ with a paired interval, and a moved mark: ▼ better, ▲ worse, ○ no change or unscored. The worst pair cell appears with its observation-level cells beside it, not only the aggregate. Unratified rows show numbers with 'unratified: no verdict' (degraded). Serves VIZ-32, EXP-31.
History sparkline of AF FNIR over dated runs, latest value labelled. It states its baseline, units, window and actual dates. Serves VIZ-24.
τ spread over the calibration folds and the FNIR range each τ gives, shown beside the single frozen τ the verdict uses. Serves EXP-30.
Refusal reason for incompatible_runs, naming the first failing check. The exit to run A's verdict is the only way out. Serves INT-24.

screens.title: S7 Clusters
screens.purpose: Clusters for each leg, in that leg's own space only. The projection is a diagnostic and never a metric map. Bench states: projection_unavailable is degraded, and the table alternative stays.

zones.label: Per-leg cluster table: pair P/R, B³ P/R, merges, fragments, unknown-absorbed, order stability. Singletons stay unassigned. Retained PCA components are shown with a variance-only spectrum and no loadings. Also show S4 Build 3 chaining_check evidence: N = all eligible held-out named-face pairs independently verified as different identities, with usable vectors in this leg; D = those pairs linked by a cluster path; C = the subset linked through a third distinct verified identity. Label D/N 'known-different path links' and C/N 'chaining_check', each with integer numerator, denominator and rate, plus held-out scope and exclusions. Read S4 clusters.json evidence, never infer identity from co-assignment. N=0 reads 'not evaluated: no eligible held-out different-identity pairs' (empty), missing evidence reads 'not evaluated: chaining evidence unavailable', and malformed evidence is error; none reads zero risk. Select a pair to inspect its path in neighbour-table. Serves VIZ-32 and [GRPH-18] Never trust the transitive closure of a raw similarity threshold (Introduction to Information Retrieval, § 17.2).

Average-linkage cosine dendrogram, cut at the production distance d = 1 − s, labelled with its cut or 'no production cut recorded'. The acceptance τ line is labelled 'acceptance τ (not a cluster cut)' at d = 1 − τ. Direct labels. Serves VIZ-40.

UMAP diagnostic projection, captioned 'diagnostic projection · distances not meaningful', with n_neighbors, min_dist and seed beside it. Claims are limited to local contiguity: no gap, density or axis claims. If the projection cannot be drawn, projection_unavailable is degraded and the neighbour table stays. Serves VIZ-18, VIZ-19. Assess any scatterplot rendering against its actual task before applying VIZ-35; diagnostic projection coordinates do not establish original-space measured extrema.

Table alternative: select a face to list its nearest neighbours in the original leg space, with their scores. Distances come from that space, not from the projection. Inspect chaining pair opens a keyboard-reachable disclosure here: pseudonymous endpoint image_id/face_id and independently verified different identity aliases, held-out fold, pair eligibility, and ordered path face/image/identity aliases with each edge score, production s threshold and link rule from S4. Mark the third identity explicitly; direct links are distinguished from third-identity chaining. No real IDs, names or pixels. Closing the disclosure restores the selected pair, leg, sort and position. This evidence remains available when projection_unavailable. Serves VIZ-18, VIZ-32, [INT-25] Map the handoffs (Microinteractions, ch. 6) and [GRPH-18] Never trust the transitive closure of a raw similarity threshold (Introduction to Information Retrieval, § 17.2).

screens.title: S8 Frames and power
screens.purpose: What each frame can claim: units, identities, PSUs, deff, n_eff, admissibility tag and MDE per step. Shows decision-manifest status without a seal value unless the manifest is ratified. Bench states: unratified is degraded and reads 'unratified: no seal shown'.

zones.label: Frame table, one row per frame: units, identities, PSUs, deff, n_eff, admissible-as tag (diagnostic, development or confirmatory), MDE per step. deff uses planning ICC 0.10 as delegated project policy, not observed ICC; show sensitivity at 0.05/0.10/0.20. Show the global floor of 50 independent PSUs separately from the pair-cell floor of 30; check the global floor before FPIR intervals. Floors do not establish power, MDE adequacy, resolvability or exhaustive GT. Golden-150 is marked verification-biased. A frame not yet acquired reads 'not acquired' and claims nothing. Serves VIZ-32, VIZ-23.

Decision manifest status: ratified and sealed (date, short hash, count of dated disconfirmers), or unratified (degraded, 'unratified: no seal shown'). Delegated project policy is declared before outcomes: k=5 identity/PSU-disjoint rotating folds (seed 2406466110), gallery seed 2468935812, paired cluster percentile bootstrap n_boot=10000 (seed 2429382368), label queue seed 336880394. Policy is not ratification; measured frame/template hashes, actual timestamps, genuine observation references and signatures stay unresolved until supplied. Queue tooling loads delegated gold/repeat shares 0.10/0.10, repeat agreement 0.90, Cohen kappa 0.80, independent-gold accuracy 0.90, support >=20 gold decisions per annotator and >=20 repeats per evaluated field; these remain hidden from L1. These are project QC defaults, not accuracy guarantees; real tier-(a) imports always require a genuine resolvable observation reference, documented applicability to the current measurement context and valid supported QC. No fixture flag bypasses the production gate; controlled generated-fixture helper output is synthetic and ineligible for real analysis. Preserve original answers and failed QC; a corrected version needs its own fresh independently blinded QC run or supported qualified SME resolution under S7, never worker deletion or revised historical QC. Reuse observation after documenting continuing applicability; unrelated version changes alone need no new human observation, while material changes beyond the observed scope or uncertainty block analysis pending a new bounded observation. Semantic created_at follows MCP 16773: seal.sealed_at, else ratification.ratified_at, else explicit ISO8601 literal. Seal and ratification may differ; a supplied explicit literal must match the highest-priority derived instant. Missing/invalid semantic dates or conflicting explicit literals raise FrameContractError. Actual attempt/private unseal-ledger consumed_at stays separate at the non-replayable receipt boundary; no clock fallback or substitution of a seal date. Serves INT-21.

screens.title: L1 Occlusion label queue
screens.purpose: Single-file HTML that the operator labels from pixels, one face box at a time. Captions, detector boxes and model names are never shown. The annotator sees position and progress only. skipped_nonresponse is the only item state the annotator sees. Other item roles are internal and never rendered on this screen.

zones.label: Full image with no detector boxes and no caption. Confirmed boxes appear only when the queue entry carries show_confirmed_boxes. The header shows position and progress only. empty: the queue has no items. error: the image fails to embed, and the item stays in the queue. Serves FORM-11.

Per face: a box mark ✓, and an occluder set chosen from m mask, s sunglasses, h hand, o object, x mixed, n none, ? can't tell. Region controls for eyes, nose and mouth cycle through visible, occluded, out-of-frame and uncertain. Only these values can be entered. Every shortcut has a visible labelled button with the same action, reachable by Tab and activated with Enter or Space. Every focusable control shows a visible :focus-visible indicator. Serves FORM-11.

Add missed face is a mode. a enters it with a visible 'drawing a box' banner. Enter or the visible Commit box button commits the box. Esc or the visible Cancel draw button cancels and restores the unchanged item; the banner disappears on exit. Button and shortcut paths agree. u marks an unknown person as a face attribute, not a second mode; at most one mode is active. Serves INT-23.

Outside draw mode: Enter next, Esc undo, skip recorded as nonresponse. A skipped item shows ○ skipped, the only item state the annotator sees, and stays in the export. The loop ends at the last item or on an explicit export. Progress reads 'done n · skipped m'. No timer advances an item; only Enter, skip or export moves the annotator on. Serves INT-24, PERC-10.
Export JSON writes the labelled items to the private output path. Nothing is imported here. A failed export keeps every label, shows the error and offers a retry. Serves INT-25.

screens.title: Back to run A verdict (compare refused)
screens.purpose: The only exit from incompatible_runs on S6. Opens run A's S1 verdict, with no comparison shown. Intentional static exit marker, with no independent content or asynchronous work. S6 error/refusal-reason owns the refusal; back-to-run-a hands off to s1-verdict, whose states own the destination. It has no separate loading, empty or error screen. [RLSE-04] Undesigned state is a bug (practice label): screen-state trigger does not apply to this marker.

flows.label: verdict → pair cell → failures → back (sort and filter kept, INT-25)
frame inspected before the verdict; development evidence is not confirmatory
verdict → stage ledger → failures at the stage → back to ledger
compatible runs compare to a Δ with its interval

steps.branch_label: select run B from compatible runs
Δ with paired interval and history

not_doing: A winner shown while a decision is unratified, inconclusive or unresolvable
Confirmatory-frame acquisition, or any confirmatory-claim UI
Label import from any screen; import stays a CLI step
Real names, real pixels or private file contents in the map or its render
A tenth screen; the nine seeds are the whole inventory
Hand-written Markdown; the rendered .md comes from the canvas CLI
